wand_of_cure_minor_wounds.name: wand of cure minor wounds
wand_of_cure_minor_wounds.lore: The Samaritan on the Jericho road treated a beaten stranger with what he had in his saddlebag: oil to soothe and wine to clean. Hedge-healers bind that same roadside mercy into a pale stick. It closes cuts and takes the ache out of bruises, and not much more.

wand_of_cure_light_wounds.name: wand of cure light wounds
wand_of_cure_light_wounds.lore: The Knights of the Hospital of St. John kept a ward in Jerusalem where pilgrims of any faith were fed on white bread and laid in clean beds. The brothers called the sick 'our lords'. Their field wands knit a slashed arm or a cracked rib well enough to walk on.

wand_of_healing.name: wand of healing
wand_of_healing.lore: Pliny wrote that the druids of Gaul climbed the sacred oak in white robes and cut its mistletoe with a golden sickle, calling the plant 'all-heal'. A rod cut from such a tree keeps the slow strength of the oak. Deep wounds close under it as bark closes over a scar.

wand_of_greater_healing.name: wand of greater healing
wand_of_greater_healing.lore: Galen of Pergamon learned surgery stitching gladiators, and called their wounds his windows into the body. He lost far fewer fighters than the physician before him and went on to treat emperors. This rod carries the arena surgeon's craft: a man run through stands up again.

wand_of_full_restoration.name: wand of full restoration
wand_of_full_restoration.lore: Asclepius, son of Apollo and pupil of the centaur Chiron, grew so skilled that he began calling the dead back. Hades complained that his kingdom was emptying, and Zeus ended the physician with a thunderbolt. The rod stops just short of that offence. Nearly everything short of death, it undoes.

wand_of_fire_spark.name: wand of fire sparks
wand_of_fire_spark.lore: Six Vestal Virgins tended Rome's hearth fire, and if it ever died they had to kindle it again by rubbing wood on wood. An apprentice's ash stick does the kindling for them: a spit of orange sparks, hot enough to sting a rat and singe a careless sleeve.

wand_of_fire_bolt.name: wand of fire bolt
wand_of_fire_bolt.lore: The defenders of Saguntum hurled the falarica at Hannibal's men: a heavy javelin with its iron shank wrapped in pitch-soaked tow and set alight. A soldier whose shield caught one had to throw the shield away. The journeyman's wand throws the same answer without the javelin.

wand_of_fireball.name: wand of fireball
wand_of_fireball.lore: Around the year 672 a refugee architect named Kallinikos brought Constantinople a liquid fire that pumped through bronze tubes and went on burning on the sea. It destroyed two Arab fleets, and the recipe was guarded so closely that it is lost. This wand keeps the result: a rolling burst no water quenches.

wand_of_fire_storm.name: wand of fire storm
wand_of_fire_storm.lore: On Mount Carmel the prophet Elijah drenched his altar three times with water and prayed once. Fire fell and consumed the bull, the wood, the stones, and the dust, and licked the trench dry. A senior pyromancer's rod calls down a column of that kind, and leaves the wall behind the target black.

wand_of_cataclysm.name: wand of cataclysm
wand_of_cataclysm.lore: Phaethon begged to drive his father's sun chariot for a single day and could not hold the horses. They plunged so low that Libya burned to desert and the rivers boiled, until Zeus struck the boy from the sky. The tip of this rod glows white before it fires. What follows is Phaethon's afternoon, aimed.

wand_of_static_spark.name: wand of static spark
wand_of_static_spark.lore: Thales of Miletus noticed that amber rubbed with fur pulls at straw and feathers. The Greeks called amber elektron, and the word has outlived them. An apprentice stormweaver's stick stores a little more than a rubbed bead does: a snapping blue arc that lifts hair and makes small creatures yelp.

wand_of_lightning_bolt.name: wand of lightning bolt
wand_of_lightning_bolt.lore: In 1752 Benjamin Franklin flew a silk kite into a thundercloud and drew sparks from a key on the string, proving lightning and the spark from amber to be one thing. He then invented the rod that leads it safely to earth. This copper wand leads it the other way, in a straight line through whatever stands there.

wand_of_chain_lightning.name: wand of chain lightning
wand_of_chain_lightning.lore: Capaneus scaled the walls of Thebes shouting that not even Zeus could stop him. Zeus stopped him on the ladder with a single thunderbolt. The bolt from this wand does not care how many stand in its path. It runs through all of them and leaves each one stunned.

wand_of_thunderstorm.name: wand of thunderstorm
wand_of_thunderstorm.lore: Near Geismar stood an oak sacred to the thunder god Donar, and around 723 the missionary Boniface took an axe to it. The crowd waited for the lightning. None came, and he built a chapel from the timber. Master stormweavers still prize thunder-oak. The air smells of struck metal when this one fires.

wand_of_zeus_wrath.name: wand of Zeus's wrath
wand_of_zeus_wrath.lore: Three Cyclopes, Brontes, Steropes and Arges, forged the thunderbolt for Zeus in thanks for their release from Tartarus. With it he broke the Titans and buried Typhon. The wand's bolt is white, silent for an eye-blink, and then arrives with a crack that rattles teeth along the whole corridor.

wand_of_chill.name: wand of chill
wand_of_chill.lore: Boreas, the north wind, lived in a cave in Thrace, and the Athenians built him an altar after his gale wrecked four hundred Persian ships off Cape Sepias. An apprentice's frost wand holds one of his lesser breaths. Fingers go numb, and whatever it touches moves stiffly for a few steps.

wand_of_cold_bolt.name: wand of cold bolt
wand_of_cold_bolt.lore: The Norse counted the frost giants, the Hrimthursar, as the oldest enemies of the gods, a race that dripped into being from melting rime. Journeymen say their spears were icicles. This wand throws a single shard of that cold. Frost crusts the skin where it lands, and the limbs behind it slow.

wand_of_frost.name: wand of frost
wand_of_frost.lore: Before there was a world, the Norse said, there was Niflheim to the north, all mist and ice, and a yawning gap called Ginnungagap where its rime met the sparks of the south. The shaft of this wand is cold in any season. Its bolt carries the old dark of that place and leaves a body sluggish.

wand_of_blizzard.name: wand of blizzard
wand_of_blizzard.lore: Fimbulwinter comes before the end, the Eddas say: three winters with no summer between them, snow driving from every quarter, and brother turning on brother for a crust. The wand lets a little of it out at a time. A howl of ice needles fills the passage, and the survivors walk away slowly.

wand_of_absolute_zero.name: wand of absolute zero
wand_of_absolute_zero.lore: In 1848 Lord Kelvin worked out that cold has a floor: a point some 273 degrees below freezing where the motion of matter stops. Dante had guessed the same about the pit of Hell, which he made a frozen lake. Master cryomancers reach for that floor. For one instant the target nearly gets there.

wand_of_acid_sting.name: wand of acid sting
wand_of_acid_sting.lore: In 1671 the naturalist John Ray boiled down a great heap of red ants and collected a sour, biting liquor, the first acid ever taken from an animal. Alchemists call it spirit of ants. Their cantrip stick squirts a drop of something similar, which raises welts and leaves a lingering sickness.

wand_of_acid_spray.name: wand of acid spray
wand_of_acid_spray.lore: Livy says that when a rock face blocked Hannibal's army in the Alps, his engineers heated the stone with great fires and doused it with sour wine until it crumbled. The wand skips the bonfire. A spreading green spray hisses on scale and plate, and whatever it wets sickens.

wand_of_acid_blast.name: wand of acid blast
wand_of_acid_blast.lore: The bombardier beetle keeps two chemicals in separate chambers of its abdomen. Mixed, they boil, and the beetle fires the scalding spray from a turret it can aim over its own back. Some alchemist studied the insect closely. Stone pits where the drops fall, and flesh fares worse.

wand_of_corrosion.name: wand of corrosion
wand_of_corrosion.lore: The dying centaur Nessus gave Deianira his blood as a love charm. It was tainted with the Hydra's venom, and when Heracles put on the shirt she had smeared with it, the cloth ate into him and would not come off. This wand carries the same clinging ruin, and the sickness after it lasts.

wand_of_dissolution.name: wand of dissolution
wand_of_dissolution.lore: Paracelsus named it and van Helmont sought it for years: the alkahest, a solvent that would dissolve anything. Johann Kunckel asked the obvious question, which was what jar they meant to keep it in. Nobody answered him. This wand does not hold the alkahest either, but armour, hide and bone have trouble telling.

wand_of_force_dart.name: wand of force dart
wand_of_force_dart.lore: The slingers of the Balearic Islands were the best in the ancient world. Their mothers, the story goes, set a boy's bread on a post and let him eat only when he had knocked it off with a stone. An apprentice's wand throws a small hard dart of nothing at all, which no armour turns.

wand_of_magic_missile.name: wand of magic missile
wand_of_magic_missile.lore: Odin's spear Gungnir was made by the dwarf sons of Ivaldi, and it had one property that mattered: once thrown, it could not miss. The standard mage's wand copies that property and nothing else. Its bolt of force goes around cover, through smoke, and into the thing it was pointed at.

wand_of_force_barrage.name: wand of force barrage
wand_of_force_barrage.lore: At Crecy in 1346 the English archers loosed so fast that a chronicler said the arrows fell like snow. The Genoese crossbowmen opposite got off one volley and broke. This wand answers a charging enemy the same way, with one bolt after another and no gap in which to raise a shield.

wand_of_force_storm.name: wand of force storm
wand_of_force_storm.lore: When Odysseus came home in rags, the test was his own bow: string it, and shoot through the sockets of twelve axe heads set in a row. He did both sitting down, and then turned to the suitors. Master abjurers favour this wand for the one enemy who must not get up.

wand_of_force_cataclysm.name: wand of force cataclysm
wand_of_force_cataclysm.lore: Archimedes told King Hiero that with a place to stand he could move the earth, and then proved the smaller claim: seated on the beach, he drew a loaded ship up the sand with one hand and a set of pulleys. Force magic at its height works the same way. The hand barely moves.

wand_of_rap.name: wand of rap
wand_of_rap.lore: Roman schoolmasters kept order with the ferula, the dried stalk of the giant fennel, light in the hand and smart on the knuckles. The poet Martial called it the sceptre of teachers. Someone enchanted this one to strike well above its weight. It is best used on things that cannot rap back.

wand_of_striking.name: wand of striking
wand_of_striking.lore: At Horeb the people cried out for water, and Moses struck the rock with his staff and water came. A journeyman evoker's wand strikes with less purpose but real weight. The tip flashes, and the blow lands as if from a war hammer that nobody in the room is holding.

wand_of_slam.name: wand of slam
wand_of_slam.lore: The Romans hung a beam from chains under a wheeled shed, capped it with a bronze ram's head, and swung. By custom, a town that surrendered before the ram touched the wall was spared. The wand makes no such offer. Its blow cracks shields and dents the breastplate behind them.

wand_of_smite.name: wand of smite
wand_of_smite.lore: At Lehi the Philistines came for Samson, and the Spirit of the Lord came on him first. He picked up the fresh jawbone of a donkey and struck down a thousand men with it. The wand needs no jawbone. Its blow falls as if a righteous arm were behind it, and armour buckles inward.

wand_of_devastation.name: wand of devastation
wand_of_devastation.lore: Thor once swung Mjolnir three times at the head of a sleeping giant, who woke and asked if a leaf had fallen on him. The giant had slipped a mountain in the way, and the three blows left three square valleys in it. This rod strikes like that, and the stone behind the target keeps the shape.

wand_of_drowsing.name: wand of drowsing
wand_of_drowsing.lore: Hera set Argus, who had a hundred eyes, to guard the heifer Io. Hermes sat down beside him, played the reed pipes, and told a long story until every eye had closed. A hedge-witch's wand works the same trick more quickly. The eyelids drop for a short while, and a blow wakes the sleeper.

wand_of_sleep.name: wand of sleep
wand_of_sleep.lore: Hera once bribed Hypnos, the god of sleep, with the hand of one of the Graces, and he perched in a pine on Mount Ida and put Zeus himself under while the war at Troy went her way. The wand has that confidence. Its target folds where it stands and stays down until hurt.

wand_of_deep_slumber.name: wand of deep slumber
wand_of_deep_slumber.lore: The valkyrie Brynhild gave victory to the wrong king, and Odin pricked her with the sleep-thorn and left her on a mountain inside a ring of fire. She lay there in her armour until Sigurd rode through the flames and cut the mail from her. This wand lays a sleep of that kind on even great beasts.

wand_of_slow.name: wand of slow
wand_of_slow.lore: Atalanta would marry only the man who could outrun her, and nobody could. Hippomenes carried three golden apples from Aphrodite and dropped one each time she drew ahead. She stooped for all three and lost. The apprentice's wand is the apple: for a little while the target cannot keep its pace.

wand_of_torpor.name: wand of torpor
wand_of_torpor.lore: On the tenth day out from Troy, Odysseus landed among the Lotus-Eaters. The men who tasted the fruit lost all wish to row, to report, or to go home, and he had to drag them back weeping and tie them under the benches. This wand feeds an enemy the same fruit. Its blows arrive a beat late.

wand_of_time_halt.name: wand of time halt
wand_of_time_halt.lore: Oisin rode to Tir na nOg, the Land of the Young, and stayed what felt like three years. When he came home, three hundred had passed in Ireland and everyone he knew was dust. The wand bends time the same way around one enemy. It still moves, as honey moves, and the bearer can afford patience.

wand_of_bewilderment.name: wand of bewilderment
wand_of_bewilderment.lore: In the west of England a traveller who lost the path in a field he knew was said to be pixy-led. The cure was to turn his coat inside out. The prankster's wand does the pixies' work, and few monsters wear coats. For a short spell the target cannot tell which way is forward.

wand_of_confusion.name: wand of confusion
wand_of_confusion.lore: The builders at Babel meant their tower to reach heaven. One morning each crew found that it could no longer understand the next, the bricks stopped moving, and the people scattered over the earth. The wand does to one mind what was done to that plain. The target reels and swings at whatever is nearest.

wand_of_madness.name: wand of madness
wand_of_madness.lore: When the armour of Achilles went to Odysseus, Ajax set out by night to kill the Greek chiefs. Athena clouded his eyes, and he spent his rage on a flock of sheep, sure they were the kings. He woke among the carcasses. This wand unseats a mind as thoroughly, and for a long while.

wand_of_hold.name: wand of hold
wand_of_hold.lore: Theseus and Pirithous went down to carry off the queen of the dead. Hades welcomed them politely and offered them seats. The stone held them fast, and Theseus sat there until Heracles came and tore him loose. An apprentice binder's wand offers the same chair, though only for a moment.

wand_of_paralysis.name: wand of paralysis
wand_of_paralysis.lore: The angels told Lot's household to run from Sodom and not look behind them. His wife looked, and stood there as a pillar of salt. Guides by the Dead Sea still point out a column and give it her name. A creature caught by this wand stops as she did, mid-step, until the hold breaks.

wand_of_petrifaction.name: wand of petrifaction
wand_of_petrifaction.lore: Niobe boasted that her fourteen children made her greater than Leto, who had two. Leto's two were Apollo and Artemis. When the arrows stopped, Niobe wept until she hardened into a rock on Mount Sipylus, and the rock still drips. The wand gives flesh that same stillness for as long as its hold lasts.

wand_of_terror.name: wand of terror
wand_of_terror.lore: Ares drove to war with his two sons at the chariot yoke: Phobos, who is Fear, and Deimos, who is Dread. In 1877 an astronomer gave their names to the two small moons of Mars. A hedge-witch's fright-stick carries a whisper of the elder brother. Courage leaves the target and it looks for a door.

wand_of_fear.name: wand of fear
wand_of_fear.lore: The dragon Fafnir wore the Helm of Awe as he lay on his gold, and no living thing dared come near him. Sigurd took it from the hoard along with the treasure. Icelanders later drew its eight-armed sign between their brows. The wand casts that dread at one enemy, which drops everything and runs.

wand_of_panic_wave.name: wand of panic wave
wand_of_panic_wave.lore: The Greeks blamed sudden, causeless terror on the goat-god Pan, whose shout from the hills could stampede a herd or an army. They said he routed the Persians at Marathon, and they named the feeling after him: panic. This wand gives the shout. Everything in sight short of the mightiest bolts for the exits.

wand_of_dimming.name: wand of dimming
wand_of_dimming.lore: The men of Sodom crowded Lot's doorway meaning harm to his guests. The guests were angels. They pulled Lot inside and struck the mob with blindness, so that the men wore themselves out groping for the door. A hedge-mage's wand fogs the eyes the same way, briefly.

wand_of_blindness.name: wand of blindness
wand_of_blindness.lore: On Cyprus a sorcerer named Elymas tried to turn the Roman governor away from the preaching of Paul. Paul looked straight at him and said he would be blind for a season. A mist fell on the man, and he went about looking for someone to lead him by the hand. The wand repeats the sentence.

wand_of_dark_curse.name: wand of dark curse
wand_of_dark_curse.lore: The ninth plague of Egypt was a darkness that could be felt. For three days no one saw his neighbour or rose from his place, though the Israelites had light where they lived. This wand lays that darkness on a single creature. To it the world is simply gone, and stays gone a long time.

wand_of_rebuke.name: wand of rebuke
wand_of_rebuke.lore: A priest blesses water with a prayer that every unclean spirit flee the place where it is sprinkled, and medieval parishes kept the font under lock so that nobody would steal it. A novice's wand carries the same blessing. The walking dead in sight are scalded by its light and turn away.

wand_of_turn_undead.name: wand of turn undead
wand_of_turn_undead.lore: In 1614 the Church gathered its prayers of exorcism into one book, the Roman Ritual, and the rite stood almost unchanged for three and a half centuries. A senior cleric's wand holds its commands of departure. Dead things that hear them burn with holy fire and flee as fast as they can.

wand_of_sunburst.name: wand of sunburst
wand_of_sunburst.lore: At the Easter Vigil the church stands dark until one new fire is struck outside the door. A deacon carries the flame up the aisle and three times sings that this is the light of Christ. The rod looses that moment whole. Lesser dead are unmade where they stand, and the greater ones run.

wand_of_small_polymorph.name: wand of small polymorph
wand_of_small_polymorph.lore: The boy Gwion tasted three drops from Ceridwen's cauldron and ran. He became a hare, and she a greyhound; he a fish, and she an otter; he a bird, and she a hawk; he a grain of wheat, and she a hen. A journeyman's wand runs one leg of that chase. Nobody chooses what comes out.

wand_of_polymorph.name: wand of polymorph
wand_of_polymorph.lore: Proteus, the Old Man of the Sea, knew everything and would tell nothing unless he was held. Menelaus seized him among his seals, and he became a lion, a serpent, a leopard, a boar, running water and a tall tree before he gave in. The wand turns a creature into another creature. Better or worse is luck.

wand_of_curse_of_the_menagerie.name: wand of curse of the menagerie
wand_of_curse_of_the_menagerie.lore: Ovid finished his Metamorphoses about the year 8 and filled it with some two hundred and fifty changes of shape. Lycaon the tyrant became a wolf, Arachne the weaver a spider, the hunter Actaeon a stag before his own hounds. This rod adds a line to the poem. Only the mightiest are spared the rewriting.

wand_of_charm.name: wand of charm
wand_of_charm.lore: A wolf was killing the people of Gubbio, and Francis of Assisi walked out alone to meet it. He called it Brother Wolf and proposed a bargain: the town would feed it, and it would harm no one. The wolf put its paw in his hand. This wand makes the same peace, for a while.

wand_of_greater_charm.name: wand of greater charm
wand_of_greater_charm.lore: When Orpheus sang, trees pulled up their roots to come closer and rivers stopped to listen. He walked into the underworld with a lyre, and Cerberus lay down, the Furies wept, and Hades agreed to give back his wife. A master enchanter's wand holds one of his songs. Hardened things stand and listen.

wand_of_dominion.name: wand of dominion
wand_of_dominion.lore: An old legend says the archangel Michael brought King Solomon a ring engraved with a seal, and that with it the king commanded the demons themselves and set them to cutting stone for the Temple. The rod borrows the seal's authority. Its target does not merely soften; it waits on the bearer as a subject.

wand_of_candle_light.name: wand of candle light
wand_of_candle_light.lore: For centuries the Church held that altar candles should be made of beeswax, because bees were thought pure and the flame burned clean. A parish chandler's stub is the model for this apprentice wand. It casts a small warm circle, enough to show the next few paces of floor and what is standing on them.

wand_of_torch_light.name: wand of torch light
wand_of_torch_light.lore: When Hades carried off Persephone, her mother Demeter lit two pine torches at the fires of Etna and searched the earth for nine days without eating or resting. An explorer's wand burns like one of them. The tip flares, and the whole of a chamber shows itself at once.

wand_of_sunlight.name: wand of sunlight
wand_of_sunlight.lore: Helios drives the sun across the sky and misses nothing. It was Helios who told Hephaestus what his wife was doing, and Helios who told Demeter where her daughter had gone. A master's wand opens his eye over an entire floor for an instant. Every passage is seen, and things that hid unseen are stripped of it.

wand_of_wonder.name: wand of wonder
wand_of_wonder.lore: Zeus sent Pandora to mankind with a great storage jar and told her not to open it. She did, and every trouble flew out, and only Hope stayed under the lid. Erasmus mistranslated the jar as a box. Nobody knows what this wand will let out: mending, fire, sleep, or a sudden change of scenery.

wand_of_greater_wonder.name: wand of greater wonder
wand_of_greater_wonder.lore: Boethius, waiting in prison for his execution around 524, imagined Lady Fortune turning her wheel. Kings rise on one side and fall on the other, and she laughs at both. A master's wonder-wand spins the same wheel as the lesser kind, only harder. The good turns are better. Nothing else is promised.

wand_of_chaos.name: wand of chaos
wand_of_chaos.lore: Eris, goddess of strife, was the one guest not invited to the wedding of Peleus and Thetis. She rolled a golden apple among the goddesses marked 'for the fairest', and ten years of war at Troy followed. This rod is her apple. Its bearer is as surprised as its target, every time.

wand_of_digging.name: wand of digging
wand_of_digging.lore: In 1215 King John besieged Rochester Castle and set miners to dig beneath a corner of the keep. He then sent for forty of the fattest pigs in the county and burned their lard in the tunnel until the props gave way and the tower fell. The wand skips the pigs. Walls and doors around its bearer burst open.

wand_of_cancellation.name: wand of cancellation
wand_of_cancellation.lore: On Carmel four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal called on their god from morning until noon, leaping and cutting themselves, and Elijah mocked that he must be asleep. Nothing answered. This wand brings the same silence to an enemy's magic. Every ward and blessing it wore goes out at once.

wand_of_drain_magic.name: wand of drain magic
wand_of_drain_magic.lore: At Philippi a slave girl with a spirit of divination earned her owners a good living by telling fortunes. She followed Paul for days until he turned and ordered the spirit out. It left, and her owners' income left with it. The wand empties a creature of its borrowed power in the same abrupt way.

wand_of_dispel_magic.name: wand of dispel magic
wand_of_dispel_magic.lore: Pharaoh's magicians matched the first signs of Moses and Aaron. They made their own serpents, turned water to blood, and called up frogs. At the third plague, the gnats, their arts failed, and they told Pharaoh this was the finger of God. The wand ends a contest the same way: the enemy's enchantments simply stop.

wand_of_teleport_monster.name: wand of teleport monster
wand_of_teleport_monster.lore: Hephaestus once took his mother's side in a quarrel, and Zeus seized him by the foot and threw him off Olympus. He fell for a whole day and landed at sunset on the island of Lemnos. A conjurer's wand hurls a creature just as freely to some far corner of the floor. It may walk back.

wand_of_poison_monster.name: wand of poison monster
wand_of_poison_monster.lore: Heracles dipped his arrows in the gall of the Hydra, and from then on any scratch from them was fatal. One grazed the wise centaur Chiron, who was immortal and so could not die of it, and he begged to give his immortality away. The alchemist's wand is slower than those arrows but as patient.

wand_of_disease_monster.name: wand of disease monster
wand_of_disease_monster.lore: The Iliad opens with a plague. Agamemnon insulted a priest of Apollo, and the god came down from Olympus like nightfall and shot his arrows into the Greek camp for nine days, first the mules and dogs, then the men. The wand looses one arrow from that quiver. It hurts at once and goes on hurting.

wand_of_curse_monster.name: wand of curse monster
wand_of_curse_monster.lore: At the hot spring of Bath, Romans scratched their grievances on small sheets of lead, rolled them up, and threw them to the goddess Sulis. About a hundred and thirty have been fished out, most asking her to ruin whoever stole a cloak. The hexer's wand delivers such a petition: bad luck and heavy feet.

wand_of_weaken_monster.name: wand of weaken monster
wand_of_weaken_monster.lore: In the hall of Utgard-Loki, Thor was challenged to wrestle the king's old nurse, a crone named Elli. The harder he gripped, the firmer she stood, and at last she forced him down on one knee. Elli was Old Age, who throws everyone. The wand lends an enemy a few of her years.

wand_of_secret_door_detection.name: wand of secret door detection
wand_of_secret_door_detection.lore: Georgius Agricola's great book on mining, printed in 1556, shows men walking the hills with forked hazel twigs that dip over hidden veins of ore. He doubted it worked. Down here it does. The dungeoneer's wand twitches toward the false wall and the door behind it shows plainly.

wand_of_opening.name: wand of opening
wand_of_opening.lore: Herod chained Peter between two soldiers with sentries at the door. In the night an angel woke him, the chains dropped from his wrists, and the iron gate to the city opened for them by itself. A thief-mage's wand offers no angel, but every door in sight swings wide and every locked chest clicks.

wand_of_probing.name: wand of probing
wand_of_probing.lore: In 1543 Andreas Vesalius published seven books on the fabric of the human body, drawn from dissections he did with his own hands, and overturned errors that had stood since Galen. A scholar's wand makes the same honest examination without the knife. It tells how much life a creature has left and what it shrugs off.

wand_of_death_ray.name: wand of death ray
wand_of_death_ray.lore: Balor, king of the Fomorians, had one eye that killed whatever it looked at. It took four men with a polished handle to lift the lid in battle, and whole companies fell when they did. His grandson Lugh put a sling stone through it. This rod opens the eye once. Only the mightiest survive the glance, and badly.

wand_of_disintegrate.name: wand of disintegrate
wand_of_disintegrate.lore: Semele asked Zeus to come to her as he came to Hera, in his true form, and he had sworn by the Styx to grant her wish. No mortal could bear the sight. She burned to ash where she stood. The beam from this rod is a sliver of that glory, and what it touches usually ceases to be.

wand_of_life_drain.name: wand of life drain
wand_of_life_drain.lore: At the edge of the world Odysseus dug a trench and filled it with the blood of a ram and a black ewe. The shades of the dead crowded up to drink, because only the blood gave them strength enough to speak. A necromancer's wand makes the same trade: life leaves the target and arrives in the bearer.

wand_of_soul_drain.name: wand of soul drain
wand_of_soul_drain.lore: Ovid describes the striges: birds with hooked beaks and grey feathers that flew by night to the cradles of unguarded infants and fed. Roman nurses hung whitethorn in the window to keep them out. A master necromancer's wand has their appetite. It draws a great draught of an enemy's life across the room.

caduceus_wand.name: Caduceus of Hermes
caduceus_wand.unidentified_name: a golden rod entwined with two serpents
caduceus_wand.lore: The caduceus is the herald's staff of Hermes: two serpents twined about a winged rod, the sign under which messengers passed unharmed. The true emblem of medicine is the single-snake staff of Asclepius, but in 1902 the United States Army Medical Corps adopted the caduceus by mistake, and the confusion stuck. The dungeon has taken the Army's side. This rod heals, and heals well.

lantern_of_diogenes.name: Lantern of Diogenes
lantern_of_diogenes.lore: Diogenes of Sinope lived in a storage jar in the marketplace of Athens and owned a cloak, a staff and a bag. He walked the streets at noon with a lit lantern, and when asked why, said he was looking for an honest man. When Alexander the Great offered him any favour, he asked the king to stop blocking the sun. The lantern still burns. It lights a whole chamber, and it is still looking.

iron_mortar_wand.name: Baba Yaga's Iron Mortar
iron_mortar_wand.lore: Baba Yaga grinds the bones of heroes in this mortar before eating them. When wielded as a wand, it channels chaotic magic -- the effect is never the same twice.

aarons_rod.name: Aaron's Rod
aarons_rod.lore: The rod of Aaron, brother of Moses. Thrown to the ground before Pharaoh's court, it became a serpent and swallowed the serpents of Pharaoh's magicians. Later, it budded almonds overnight to settle a dispute among the tribes. From Exodus 7 and Numbers 17. Whatever an enemy raises, the rod takes the legs out from under it.

circes_wand.name: Circe's Wand
circes_wand.lore: Circe, daughter of the Sun, kept a house of polished stone on the island of Aeaea, with tame wolves and lions at the door. She gave the crew of Odysseus a drugged wine, touched them with her wand, and drove them into her sties as swine with the minds of men. Hermes gave Odysseus the herb moly, and against him her magic failed. In other hands the wand has grown careless. It still changes a creature, but into what, nobody chooses.

indras_vajra.name: Indra's Vajra
indras_vajra.lore: The Rigveda sings of the vajra, the thunderbolt that the craftsman-god Tvastr fashioned for Indra. With it Indra split open the serpent Vritra, who lay coiled on the mountains hoarding the waters, and the seven rivers ran to the sea. A later tradition says it was made from the bones of the sage Dadhichi, who gave up his body so the gods could have their weapon. Its bolt runs through everything that stands in a line.

ruby_rod.name: Ruby Rod of Asmodeus
ruby_rod.lore: In the Book of Tobit the demon Asmodeus killed seven husbands of Sarah, each on his wedding night, until the angel Raphael showed young Tobias how to drive him out with the smoke of a fish's heart and liver. Raphael chased the demon to Upper Egypt and bound him there. Later ages made him a king of Hell and gave him this sceptre. Its ruby holds a fire that has not cooled, and the rod spends it freely.
ruby_rod.design_notes: Asmodeus L92 boss drop. Wired via monster.treasure.unique_drop_id.
